Synthetic input shapes on a calendar (deterministic)

Source: R/topia.R
topia_profile.Rd

Generate a simple geometric profile – a step-wise staircase, a sine/cosine wave, or a hexagonal trapezoid – over the timeslices of a calendar, ready to use as weather (wval), availability multipliers, or demand shapes. The synthetic counterpart of the realistic topia_profiles(): where those answer "what does a year look like", these answer "what is the simplest input that isolates one mechanism" (storage bridging an on/off resource, techs following a ramp, trade smoothing opposite phases).

Usage

topia_profile(
  shape = c("step", "sine", "cosine", "hex"),
  levels = 4L,
  calendar = "s4_h24",
  regions = NULL,
  vary = c("none", "phase", "amplitude"),
  min = 0,
  max = 1,
  period = c("year", "frame"),
  phase = 0
)

Arguments

shape

"step" (ascending staircase with levels plateaus: 0, 1/(levels-1), ..., 1), "sine", "cosine", or "hex" (trapezoid ramp/plateau/ramp in equal thirds).

levels

integer >= 2, number of plateaus for shape = "step" (ignored otherwise). levels = 2 is the on/off case.

calendar

a calendar object, the name of a shipped calendar (see calendars), or a timetable data.frame.

regions

optional character vector. NULL returns the bare shape (timeslice, step, value); otherwise the shape is replicated per region with a leading region column.

vary

per-region variation (needs regions): "none" replicates identically; "phase" shifts region i by (i-1)/n of the period (a gradient across the map – neighbouring regions peak in sequence); "amplitude" scales region i's amplitude by 1 - (i-1)/(2(n-1)) (from 1 down to 1/2 – good sites to poor sites).

min, max

numeric range the unit shape is scaled to (value = min + shape * (max - min)).

period

"year" (one cycle over the calendar) or "frame" (one cycle inside each parent timeframe of the finest level).

phase

numeric, fraction of the period the shape is shifted by (applied to all regions, on top of vary = "phase" offsets).

Value

A tidy data.frame, chronologically ordered: region (only when regions is given), timeslice (the calendar's finest level), step (integer plateau index 0..levels-1 for "step", NA otherwise – the pretty-number handle for hand-checkable inputs), and value in [min, max].

Details

Despite the shared prefix, this function reads no TOPIA data and is not limited to TOPIA: it works on any calendar and returns a single data.frame. topia_profiles() (plural) is the other one – it expands TOPIA's saved weather / demand / stock to regions and returns a list of three.

The shape spans period once: "year" stretches it over the whole calendar; "frame" repeats it inside each parent timeframe (e.g. each season's hours get the same diurnal shape). Slice positions are the midpoints of each timeslice's share along the calendar's own chronological chain, so unequal slices land where they belong; the cycle's anchor is the alphabetically first timeslice (rotate with phase).

See also

topia_profiles() for the realistic TOPIA curves, topia for the reference dataset and the teaching kits.

Other topia: topia, topia_profiles()

Examples

# on/off resource on the 4-slice test calendar: free half the year
topia_profile("step", levels = 2, calendar = "s4")
#>   timeslice step value
#> 1       FAL    0     0
#> 2       WIN    0     0
#> 3       SPR    1     1
#> 4       SUM    1     1

# a diurnal sine for every season, phased across three regions
head(topia_profile("sine", calendar = "s4_h24",
                    regions = c("W1", "W2", "C1"), vary = "phase",
                    period = "frame"))
#>   region timeslice step     value
#> 1     W1   FAL_h00   NA 0.5652631
#> 2     W1   FAL_h01   NA 0.6913417
#> 3     W1   FAL_h02   NA 0.8043807
#> 4     W1   FAL_h03   NA 0.8966767
#> 5     W1   FAL_h04   NA 0.9619398
#> 6     W1   FAL_h05   NA 0.9957224
